 Print (L-R) Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj bowl at the nets in Wellington (Photos: BCCI) Wellington : The World Test Championship (WTC) final is Shubman Gill 's ultimate goal, and the target is firmly in sight for the Indian captain. Even while India were preparing for their tour of New Zealand, Gill was closely tracking the Test series between Australia and South Africa. He was well aware of how the results could affect India's chances of qualifying for next year's title clash. The race has now tightened, and India can put themselves firmly in contention with a strong showing in the two-Test series, which gets underway on Thursday. Watch Shubman Gill press conference : India's playing XI, bowling combination, Rishabh Pant & more These are arguably the two most challenging Tests for Gill, both as captain and batter, but the 27-year-old is ready to take them head-on. His batting preparations included a camp in Auckland and extended practice sessions in Wellington ahead of the series opener. Now, bold selection calls are expected when the team takes the field. For a group obsessed with batting depth, even if it has come at the cost of a wicket-taking bowler, a shift in strategy is very much on the cards at Windy Welly. Gill made it clear that India want to play four frontline fast bowlers to be better equipped for the demands of five-day Test cricket. The Indian captain does not want to be left short of options when the pitch and conditions change. "We definitely want four fast-bowling options, but we are still deciding which are those fast bowlers, and we want to cover all the aspects. We have seen at times on day three, four and five, the wicket, especially with the old ball, does go a little bit flat, so from our fast-bowling unit, we would want someone who has pace, someone who can hit the areas consistently, and then obviously going in with one spinner to control from one end, because it won't be easy to bowl against the wind if the wind is strong," he said. "The fast bowler's role is almost cut into half, especially someone who is bowling against the wind, so there are a lot of factors that we are going to take into consideration," added Gill. Gurnoor Brar is also in the mix to make his Test debut. (Photo: BCCI) India have six bowlers competing for the four spots, with even Nitish Kumar Reddy in contention. While Gill did not name anyone, he offered a clear insight into the team's thinking for the series. Jasprit Bumrah , Prasidh Krishna, Anshul Kamboj and Akash Deep are the frontrunners. Gurnoor Brar cannot be ignored either. He is in red-hot form and was a late addition to the Test squad following his impressive performances in the ODI series. Both Anshul and Akash can contribute with the bat from the No. 8 and No. 9 positions, respectively, as the team management considers going in with seven specialist batting options. Ideally, we are looking at seven proper batsmen, and then the eight and nine would be depending on... Akash can bat a bit, Anshul can bat a bit.
 Shubman Gill "Ideally, we are looking at seven proper batsmen, and then the eight and nine would be depending on... Akash can bat a bit, Anshul can bat a bit. Even if we go with Reddy, he is a proper batsman, so we will see what kind of combination we want to go with and what exactly we want to do," said Gill. The draw against Sri Lanka in Colombo hurt India's chances, but Gill is well aware of the qualification calculations and understands the importance of winning these two Tests before taking on Australia in a five-Test series at home next year.  "I believe that if we win these two Test matches, we will have a very good chance of reaching the WTC final. That was our focus even before arriving here. I knew these two matches would be crucial to our chances of qualifying for next year's final, which is why we pulled most of our players out of the ODI squad to ensure they had the best possible preparation and give ourselves the best chance of winning both games," emphasised Gill. India have given themselves the best possible chance with thorough preparation for the New Zealand challenge. Most members of the squad have had sufficient game time through India A fixtures, while the entire group has been training at the Basin Reserve since November 12. With greater clarity on selection, the focus now shifts to the wind, the 15mm grass covering the pitch, the grey skies and what promises to be an exciting contest between bat and ball.
